::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Linewidth resets when using input files](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/31213/linewidth-resets-when-using-input-files), asked by [adn](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/7561/adn) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-10-11; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I'm trying to set some figure files in standalone .tex files, and then input them in the main file. Those files looks something like this
>
> ```latex
> \ifx \plotwidth \undefined
>  \newlength{\plotwidth} \setlength{\plotwidth}{0.9\linewidth} 
> \else \fi% width of the total figure
> \rule{\linewidth}{\plotwidth}% figure goes here
> ```
>
> The main idea I have is to set standard widths using `\linewidth`, and being able to change the size in the main file by defining the `\plotwidth` before inputting the file. However, when I call the figures the second time in the same file, for some reason the `\plotwidth` is defined but its lenght is zero. As this example show
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
>
> \begin{document}
>
> \begin{figure}
> \input{fig.tex}
> \caption{Test}
> \end{figure}
>
> \begin{figure}
> \input{fig.tex}
> \caption{Test}
> \end{figure}
>
> \end{document}
> ```
> Can someone explain me why this is not working, and how to solve it?
:::

The problem is that `\newlength` is global but `\setlength` is local.  The first time your main document inputs fig.tex `\plotwidth` is undefined so the new length is created and set.  This happens inside a TeX group so the setting is local to the input file.  Then that group ends and `\plotwidth` reverts to its initial setting of `0.0pt`.

The second time the name document inputs fig.tex `\plotwidth` *is* defined, so the `\setlength` branch is not expanded.  The result is that `\plotwidth` remains at `0.0pt`.

The solution is to give `\plotwidth` a value in the main tex file.  

Also, if you want your `fig.tex` file to be standalone tex file, the easiest way to do that is to use the `standalone` document class and package.  Here is your MWE with that:

fig.tex:

```latex
\documentclass{standalone}
\begin{document}
\ifx \plotwidth \undefined
 \newlength{\plotwidth} \setlength{\plotwidth}{0.9\linewidth} 
\else \fi% width of the total figure

\rule{\plotwidth}{\plotwidth}% figure goes here
\end{document}
```

main.tex:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{standalone}

\newlength{\plotwidth} \setlength{\plotwidth}{0.5\linewidth}
\begin{document}

\begin{figure}
\include{fig}
\caption{Test}
\end{figure}


\begin{figure}
\include{fig}
\caption{Test}
\end{figure}

\end{document}
```

`\showthe\plotwidth` in your file will halt expansion and show you the current value of `\plotwidth`.  Very good for debugging.

I notice as I finish this that egreg has answered as well.  I basically agree with him.
